title: Famous rivers.
lede: The record-breakers, the rivers of the world's capitals and Britain's cities, and a few from history and myth, down to the five rivers of the Greek underworld.

card.title: Famous rivers
card.desc: The longest, the deepest, the rivers of the great cities, and the five rivers of the underworld.

extras.title: The Grand River Cruise
extras.desc: A vintage travel-poster voyage. Sail from city to city, collecting a poster for every river you name.

items.known: The world's longest river; flows through Cairo and Khartoum
items.hook: The usual answer, though some surveys measure the Amazon as longer. The Blue and White Niles meet at Khartoum.

items.length: About a fifth of all the river water reaching the world's seas
items.hook: More water than the next several biggest rivers put together.

items.known: Crosses the most countries (10) and four capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade
items.hook: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, Belgrade: 'Very Brave Bears Bathe'.

items.length: About 6,300 km: third longest in the world

items.hook: Romulus and Remus were found on its bank.

items.known: London; the longest river in England
items.hook: Longest wholly in England; the Severn is longer but starts in Wales.

items.known: Baghdad; with the Euphrates, the river of Mesopotamia

items.hook: It also flows past the Taj Mahal at Agra.

items.known: The longest river in the UK
items.length: About 354 km, from Wales to the Bristol Channel
Engineers reversed it in 1900 to carry the city's sewage away from Lake Michigan

items.known: Julius Caesar crossed it in 49 BC
items.length: Leading his army into Italy meant civil war; hence 'crossing the Rubicon', the point of no return
items.hook: 'The die is cast', he is supposed to have said.

items.known: With the Tigris, the river of Mesopotamia
items.hook: Mesopotamia is Greek for 'between the rivers': the Tigris and the Euphrates.

items.known: Greek underworld: the river of hatred
items.length: The gods swore their unbreakable oaths by it

items.known: Greek underworld: the river of woe
items.length: Charon ferried the souls of the dead across it

items.known: Greek underworld: the river of forgetfulness
items.length: The dead drank from it to forget their lives

items.known: Greek underworld: the river of fire
Greek underworld: the river of wailing
